package_info.package_versions: Outdated Magento CMS installations (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The ATMZOW Magecart script is malicious because it is injected into e-commerce sites running outdated Magento CMS, with the explicit purpose of stealing sensitive payment and donor information by intercepting and exfiltrating form data entered by users.

execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript in payment/donation page (Magento CMS template or static block)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code intercepts form submissions on payment/donation pages, collects all entered data, and exfiltrates it via an HTTP POST request to a hardcoded malicious domain, resulting in theft of sensitive user information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating form data to an external, non-legitimate domain is a classic sign of Magecart-style skimming attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal e-commerce JavaScript should not send payment or donor data to third-party domains outside of trusted payment processors.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment integrations may send data to trusted third-party services, but only with user consent and to known, reputable endpoints.
key_indicators: Form data exfiltration to unknown external domain
No user notification or consent for data transfer

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits outdated Magento CMS to gain access and inject malicious JavaScript (ATMZOW Magecart script) into payment/donation pages.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present on the site and ready to execute when users interact with forms.

attack_chain.action: When a user submits a payment or donation form, the injected JavaScript intercepts the form submission.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive form data is captured by the malicious script.

attack_chain.action: The script exfiltrates the captured data to a remote attacker-controlled server via HTTP POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment/donor information for further abuse or sale.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code intercepting form submissions and sending data to external domains
Unexpected network requests from client-side code during form submission
Presence of obfuscated or unauthorized scripts in payment/donation page templates
file_indicators: Injected JavaScript in Magento CMS templates or static blocks
References to external domains not associated with legitimate payment processors
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the site or known payment providers
Outbound connections from client browsers to suspicious or newly registered domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor e-commerce and donation pages for unauthorized JavaScript that intercepts form submissions and sends data to unknown external domains. Use web application firewalls (WAF) to detect and block suspicious outbound requests. Regularly audit CMS templates and static blocks for injected or obfuscated scripts, and monitor for changes to files associated with payment workflows.
